title: Sharp universal death of entanglement threshold for Pauli Hamiltonians
abstract: We determine the exact universal high-temperature separability threshold for Pauli Hamiltonians of bounded degree $Δ\ge2$. If every coefficient in the Hamiltonian has magnitude at most one and each term has overlapping support with at most $Δ$ other terms, the Gibbs state is a mixture of product Pauli eigenstates whenever \[ β\le z_Δ:= \operatorname{arctanh}\left[\max_{0\le x \le 1}x\left(\frac{1-x}{1+x}\right)^{Δ-1} \right]. \] For every $β>z_Δ$, a finite commuting Hamiltonian with maximum overlap degree at most $Δ$ has an entangled Gibbs state. At any fixed $β<z_Δ$ strictly below the threshold, a classical polynomial-time algorithm produces samples from a distribution over product Pauli eigenstates approximating the Gibbs state in trace distance.

bite.hook: Physicists found the exact universal temperature threshold where entanglement completely vanishes in Pauli Hamiltonians.
tldr: Identified the exact high-temperature threshold where quantum entanglement strictly dies in bounded-degree Pauli systems.
Derived a closed-form formula based on maximum term overlap degree and proved classical simulatability above threshold temperature.
Showed states below the critical inverse temperature are classical mixtures, while entangled states always exist above it.
bite.whyItMatters: Pinpointing when thermal noise destroys entanglement reveals the strict boundary where quantum systems become completely classical and easy for ordinary computers to simulate.
bite.eli5: Heat scrambles delicate quantum connections into ordinary noise. This paper calculates the exact temperature above which a quantum system melts into simple classical behavior that standard computers can mimic.
